question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{x}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =1-\frac{{(\pi /2)}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{(\pi /2)}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{(\pi /2)}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯ \\ 0 & =1-\frac{(\pi /2)^{2}}{2!}+\frac{(\pi /2)^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{(\pi /2)}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the sum of the series is $0.$
